title: Clear a fruit plate: apple to the bowl, then stand the knife hidden under the paper towels in a glass without going near a full mug of coffee
instruction: Someone cut fruit and left the plate like this. Put the apple in the bowl, then clear the paper towels off the plate; the fruit knife is under them. Stand the knife in the glass, blade down with the handle sticking up. Don't drop anything. The mug is full of hot coffee, so don't spill it and keep the knife well away from it.
context: Paper towels often end up hiding a knife on a kitchen counter. The robot has to infer the hidden blade, uncover it in an order that does not drop the apple, and route the knife clear of an open, full drink.
setup: Positions in mm: x forward of the line through the two arm bases, y left (+) or right (-) of the point midway between them (robot's view); heights above the table top. Arm bases at y = +305 and -305. (1) Plate, loose: white glazed ceramic disc, 220 diameter, 10 tall, 450 g, centred (260, 0). (2) Fruit knife, loose, one rigid body 170 long lying flat along y on the plate, centred (260, 0): black polypropylene handle 90 x 20 x 14 toward the right (y -85 to +5), stainless-steel blade 80 x 18 x 3 toward the left (y +5 to +85; thickened from 1.5 for simulation stability); 40 g in total. (3) Folded paper-towel pad, loose: white paper, 120 (x) x 110 (y) x 8, 3 g, centred (260, 40) on the blade and plate. (4) Paper-towel sheet, loose: white paper, 260 (x) x 240 (y) x 1.5, 4 g, centred (260, 0), covering the plate and knife; its front and back edges overhang the plate rim by 20 mm. (5) Apple, loose: red, 80 diameter, 190 g, on the sheet centred (260, 20). (6) Bowl, fixed: white ceramic, open, 150 outer diameter, 65 tall, centred (240, 260). (7) Mug, loose: white ceramic, 85 outer diameter, 95 tall, full of coffee (liquid not simulated; 380 g in total), centred (240, -170). (8) Glass, loose: clear glass tumbler, 72 outer / 64 inner diameter, 85 tall, 12 thick base, 220 g, centred (220, -300). Free table space for the towels: in front of the plate (x above 370) and between the robot and the plate on the left (x below 150). A straight path from the knife to the glass passes within 72.5 mm of the mug's axis. Friction static/dynamic: ceramic 0.5/0.4, glass 0.4/0.3, paper 0.6/0.5, polypropylene 0.6/0.5, apple skin 0.7/0.6, steel 0.4/0.3. Fixed layout, no jitter.
scoring: Judged on object poses only. Apple in bowl: apple centre within 35 mm horizontally of the bowl's axis and at most 60 mm above the table, at rest; it does not count if the apple ever touched the table top. Towels cleared: neither towel overlaps the plate or the knife, each lies within 30 mm of the table top, and neither is in or on the bowl, mug or glass. Knife in glass: knife tip inside the glass at least 10 mm below the rim. Knife set: tip at least 25 mm below the rim, handle end at least 40 mm above the rim, knife axis 12 to 45 degrees from vertical (a released knife leans on the rim; a vertical one is still being held), glass tilted at most 5 degrees and moved at most 30 mm. Tiers (end state, highest met): 1.00 apple in bowl, towels cleared, knife set, apple, knife, glass, mug and towels at rest for 1 s; 0.75 apple, towels and knife in glass but not set or not at rest; 0.50 apple and towels; 0.25 apple only; else 0. Cap 0.50 (any moment): any point of the knife, while lifted more than 15 mm above the plate, within 72.5 mm horizontally of the mug's axis (mug radius + 30 mm, at any height); or the knife falling faster than 0.8 m/s. Permanent zero (any moment, cannot be undone): mug tilted more than 8 degrees or moved more than 15 mm (coffee spilt); glass tilted more than 30 degrees; knife off the table. Every threshold is a development estimate pending calibration. The trial ends at the run limit or once 1.00 has held for 1 s.
fidelity: Rigid bodies only. Paper towels are rigid thin plates (no bending or crumpling); coffee is not simulated and spilling is proxied by the mug's tilt and displacement; the knife is one rigid compound; bowl, mug and glass are rigid hollow meshes. Which arm handles which object is not scored; the layout places the bowl on the left arm's side and the glass on the right arm's side.

reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. The towels must be laid back exactly over the plate and knife.
